journeys.summary: The core editing math is correct: fill none/solid/linear/radial transitions all work and gradients render properly (radial verified visually at test/review/shots/exp-properties4-fill-radial.png), rounded corners apply (Rx=25/Ry=18, exp-properties4-corners.png), rotation pivots around bbox center, skew composes cleanly with rotation (rotate(...) skewX(20) skewY(12)), stroke width and dash presets work, non-numeric input is correctly rejected (H=abc stayed 120), and nudge/Delete/copy work once a selection is genuinely present (5 arrow presses -> delta 5mm; Delete dropped layer kids 1->0). But the panel has real correctness bugs. HIGH: the prominent top 'Frame' X/Y/W/H/R readout NEVER refreshes after a property edit or nudge because ControlBar subscribes only to selection changes, not to history (PropertiesPanel was explicitly fixed to subscribe to history; ControlBar was not); it lies until you re-select and can show values contradicting the Position/Size panel for the identical attribute. HIGH: negative and zero W/H are accepted, writing invalid SVG (console error 'A negative value is not valid'), making the shape vanish and leaving 3 broken phantom selection handles; validation is isNaN-only with no >=0 clamp. MEDIUM: the focus-stealing trap is still present — while any input is focused the global keydown handler returns early, silently swallowing Ctrl+C/Delete/arrow-nudge until blur. MEDIUM: Frame and Position/Size are redundant duplicate coordinate editors that can disagree. LOW: the Dash 'Custom...' option is a dead no-op. Fixes are localized and mechanical (subscribe ControlBar to history; clamp numeric attrs to >=0; refine which shortcuts are suppressed in inputs; de-duplicate Frame/Position), so this is fixable rather than rework.

Add layer, reorder (up/down, undoable), and delete-down-to-last-layer (last layer correctly keeps its delete button hidden) all work. Lock/hide correctly gate the drawing tools (you cannot draw into a locked layer). BUT the panel has a cluster of state/history bugs that are the same root cause as the owner's confirmed bug #1, reached via new paths: (1) lock and hide mutate the DOM directly and push NOTHING onto the undo stack, so they are silently non-undoable; (2) because hide is not a command, pressing Ctrl+Z after hiding a layer reverts the user's *previous* edit (e.g. the rect they just drew) instead of un-hiding the layer — silent data loss from the user's mental model; (3) hiding a layer does NOT clear the selection of elements on it: a fully-handled selection box keeps rendering on top of the now-invisible shape and the inspector still says "RECT · 1 SELECTED" with editable frame values, so you can drag/resize a shape you can't see; (4) the dangling selection box from #2/#3 is the confirmed phantom-selection bug. Separately, multi-page is entirely unimplemented in the UI despite being part of this journey: the status-bar page-nav is a hardcoded "Page 1 / 1" stub with both arrow buttons permanently disabled, and the Inspector "Pages" tab is a placeholder reading "Multi-page support lands with vectorfeld-4w7." There is no rename affordance for layers at all (no double-click-to-rename, no rename input) — names are auto-assigned only. No console/page errors throughout.

The clipboard journey is mostly solid for single elements but has one real data-corruption bug for groups. What works well: Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V offsets the paste by exactly 5mm down-right (vf-1 at x=-3.82 -> vf-2 at x=1.18, +5mm) and selects the new copy (inspector 'RECT · 1 SELECTED vf-2'). Ctrl+Shift+V (paste-in-place) correctly applies NO offset (vf-3 lands at the identical x=-3.82,y=-1.17 as vf-1). Repeated Ctrl+V each adds a fresh-id copy (vf-3..vf-6, layerKids grows 2->6) with no id collisions for plain elements. Ctrl+D duplicates (kids 6->7) and selects the new copy. Ctrl+X removes the element (kids 7->6) AND cleanly clears selection (selBoxes=0, no phantom selection box — good, unlike the known undo-phantom bug), and the cut content pastes back (kids 6->7). Clipboard survives undo: after Ctrl+Z then Ctrl+V the paste still works (kids 8->9). Pasted elements are selected and editable (arrow-nudge worked on the freshly pasted copy). Cross-layer paste is correct: adding Layer 2 and pasting lands the copy on the active Layer 2, not the source Layer 1. No console errors or page errors anywhere. THE BUG: pasting or duplicating a GROUP regenerates only the top-level group's id; the group's child elements are re-inserted verbatim with their ORIGINAL ids, so the live DOM and the exported SVG end up with duplicate ids (confirmed vf-9 and vf-10 each appear twice in the exported .svg). Root cause is clipboard.ts pasteClipboard lines 84-95: after AddElementCommand creates the new top-level element with a fresh id, the parsed original's child nodes are moved over with `created.appendChild(original.firstChild)` and never get new ids. Fix: walk the transferred subtree and call generateId() for every descendant that has an id (and remap any internal url(#id) references). I could not fully test cross-PAGE paste — the document had a single page and no obvious add-page control was reachable from the Pages tab in this run; cross-layer was verified instead.

Core pen-bezier drawing actually works well: click-drag pulls smooth symmetric handles, multi-anchor S-curves render cleanly (shot exp-pen-bezier-04), open paths finish on Enter, closed paths commit with a trailing Z, and Direct Select reveals anchors and lets you drag a node or an individual control handle (which correctly edits one handle independently). Two assigned bugs are CONFIRMED with hard evidence. t7u (asymmetric handles): the pen tool has NO alt-key handling at all — onMouseMove unconditionally mirrors handleIn = 2*pos - pt, so every handle pulled with the pen is forced perfectly symmetric. I instrumented the canvas and proved Alt was genuinely held (altKey:true on every drag mousemove) yet the emitted handleIn/handleOut were still exact mirrors (relative -13.24,0 vs +13.24,0). So there is no way to author a corner/cusp or asymmetric handle with the pen — you must draw symmetric, then go into Direct Select and drag one side. 9hu (smooth S/s curves): buildPathD only ever emits absolute C commands; it never emits S/s smooth shorthand. The exported SVG contained zero S/s commands (regex check returned false) even for a textbook S-curve where S would be the natural/compact encoding. Output is geometrically correct (chained C segments) but the path data is verbose and the 'smooth' relationship between segments is not encoded, so any consumer relying on S-continuity (or a human reading the d-string) loses that information. Minor adjacent smell: after the pen auto-selects+switches to select tool on finish, the select-tool bounding box on the closed path stays rendered after switching to Direct Select on another path (visible in shots 09/10).

The underlying transform MATH is sound: numeric rotate works and preserves skew; SkX/SkY genuinely emit skewX()/skewY() (an early "skew writes rotate" reading was a test-harness misfire, disproven on re-test); uniform (Shift) scale of a 45deg-rotated square stays a perfect square (aspect 1.000); multi-select group scale anchors correctly at NW and grows both sizes and gaps; the selection box/handles correctly follow the rotated frame. The serious problem is INTERACTION, not math: each corner SCALE handle is a 10px square centered on the corner, but a 20px invisible rotation zone is appended AFTER it (so it wins hit-testing) covering the corner-facing half PLUS the exact center of every corner handle. Result: a user clicking the visible white corner handle to resize will ROTATE instead whenever they hit the center or outer half (confirmed by elementFromPoint + before/after geometry across 5 click offsets). This makes corner-scale feel broken and silently rotates shapes by tiny amounts. A secondary UX surprise: non-uniform (no-shift) drag-scale of a heavily-rotated rect collapses one axis dramatically (W 33->42, H 20->3) -- this is geometrically consistent with the local-space inverse mapping, but is jarring and offers no visual constraint feedback.

The core math is solid but the integration around groups and multi-selection is broken. WHAT WORKS: All 6 Align ops via the Object menu produce correct, equal edges/centers (verified to within 1px rounding). Distribute H works correctly via the Inspector buttons (even center spacing). Z-order via the Object menu AND keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+], Ctrl+[, Ctrl+Shift+], Ctrl+Shift+[) all reorder the DOM correctly on a SINGLE selection — no shortcut conflicts observed. Group/nest/ungroup of UNTRANSFORMED groups round-trips structurally (nesting depth and child counts are preserved). No console/page errors throughout. WHAT'S BROKEN (4 real, new bugs): (1) CRITICAL — Ungroup silently discards the group's transform, teleporting and de-rotating every child (data loss); the transform matrix is never baked into children. (2) HIGH — the selection overlay and inspector completely ignore an ancestor group's transform, so a transformed group's handles render in the wrong place and Rot reads 0; you can't manipulate a transformed group on canvas. (3) HIGH — grouping reorders children by click/selection order instead of document z-order, visibly restacking overlapping shapes (Group should never change appearance). (4) HIGH — a plain click on an already-selected element does not collapse a multi-selection to one, so you cannot drill from Ctrl+A down to a single shape; combined with z-order being enabled-but-no-op on multi-select (MEDIUM), this is a confusing dead-end. Also: Distribute is missing from the Object menu (LOW, lives only in the Inspector). NOTE: I initially suspected shift-click additive selection was broken, but that was a Playwright modifier-delivery artifact — holding Shift via keyboard.down works and marquee select works; shift-click is NOT a real bug.

Document-content undo/redo is fundamentally SOUND: a clean undo-all/redo-all cycle on a non-empty doc (rect, rect, nudge, group) round-trips with a STRICT byte-identical SVG match (test B: "STRICT XML MATCH: true"), and branch truncation works correctly (a new op after undo wipes the redo stack; a subsequent redo is a no-op). No crashes, zero console/page errors across all adversarial runs.

The entire class of defects here is ONE architectural root cause: SelectionState (src/model/selection.ts) holds raw Element references in a plain array, and CommandHistory.undo()/redo() (src/model/commands.ts lines 43-57) plus their callers in EditorContext.tsx (lines 118, 121) perform ZERO selection reconciliation on undo/redo. When undo removes an element, the selection array keeps the now-detached node, and updateOverlay() is never re-run, so phantom selection boxes/handles persist and the inspector keeps lying.

This produces three escalating bugs: (1) the confirmed phantom-selection cosmetic bug, now precisely characterized; (2) a NEW data-resurrection bug — Ctrl+D on a phantom selection serializes the detached node and pastes a live clone, materializing geometry on a document that undo had emptied (this exports into the PDF); (3) a NEW silent-no-op bug — nudge/align/group on the phantom selection do nothing while the UI insists 3 objects are selected. The fix is small and centralized: prune disconnected elements from selection (and call updateOverlay) on every undo/redo, or have undo/redo clearSelection.

Preview/overlay cleanup is actually solid: switching tools mid-operation reliably removes all [data-role="preview"] elements (rect/pen/text caret/anchors) via each tool's onDeactivate hook, and rapid V/R/T/P/A/E cycling leaves zero orphans and throws no console/page errors. The real problems are Escape semantics and inconsistent commit-vs-discard policy on tool switch. (1) NEW: Escape during a rectangle drag is a complete no-op — rectTool has no onKeyDown handler, so Escape is swallowed, the preview rect stays on canvas, and the subsequent mouseup COMMITS the rectangle anyway. There is no way to abort a rectangle once you've pressed mouse-down. Pen, by contrast, handles Escape correctly (cancels and discards). (2) NEW: Switching tools mid-operation has inconsistent semantics — rect DISCARDS the in-progress shape (onDeactivate just removes the preview), but pen and text COMMIT the in-progress element (onDeactivate calls finish()/commit()). So tool-switching mid-pen silently creates a path and mid-text silently creates a text element, while mid-rect throws the shape away. (3) Keyboard tool shortcuts cannot switch tools during text editing — because text editing sets keyboard capture, pressing r/v/p types those literal characters into the text body (produced text content 'ABrv', 'HELLOrvt'); the only ways out are Escape/Enter or clicking a tool slot with the mouse. (4) Inspector keeps showing the prior selection (RECT 1 SELECTED + visible selection-box) after switching to the Text/Pen tool, so the Text tool presents stale rect properties instead of a clean creation state. No crashes, no console errors, no stale previews in any path.

DEFINITIVE ANSWER: a non-expert user CANNOT fix a typo in a Word-generated PDF with this tool. There is no path to edit text content of an imported PDF. Root cause: PDF import wraps every text run in an intermediate <g> (each layer direct child is a <g> containing one <text>). The select-tool hit test (src/model/geometry.ts hitTestElement) only iterates DIRECT children of the layer <g>, so a click ALWAYS selects the wrapping <g>, never the inner <text>. Because the selected element is a <g>, the inspector renders generic group props: the Font section (gated on tag==='text' in PropertiesPanel.tsx:453) never appears, there is no text-content field anywhere in the app, and the fill control reports fill-type 'none' with NO color picker — so even recoloring is impossible. Double-click does nothing (there is no double-click-to-edit handler in selectTool at all). The Text tool clicked over existing text creates a brand-new empty text element (textTool.ts startEditing always resets state.text=''); it never loads the existing run, so typed text is lost and the original is untouched. Delete and Move DO operate, but only on a single fragment: text is shredded into ~one-run-per-line <g> wrappers (112 layer children, all <g>, e.g. deleting one removed only the 'Ich entlaste' prefix, leaving 'durch mein Lektorat...'). Exports are faithful to the canvas (roundtrip is solid), which only confirms that the failed edits never landed. The only console noise is the known symbolic-font subsetting warning.

The core import pipeline is sound: the editable flyer imports with full content (106 text els, 817 chars, 3 images incl. QR), the outlined flyer renders correctly (it genuinely is just a logo/header flyer, not dropped content) and is correctly tagged data-mostly-outlined=true with 216 paths / 15 chars, background-layer compositing stacks correctly (outlined behind, editable text on top), and Open SVG / re-import-replace behave as designed. NO console/page errors throughout. BUT there is a systemic stale-refresh bug in the two primary "replace" import paths (Open PDF..., Open SVG...): both call clearSelection() — the LayersPanel's only refresh trigger — BEFORE they mutate the layer DOM, so the panel reads pre-import state and never updates. Consequences: (A) the mostly-outlined warning badge does NOT appear when you import the outlined PDF via the normal Open PDF... menu — the entire purpose of the feature is defeated for the most common path (the background-layer path works because it deliberately fires clearSelection LAST); (C) after Open SVG the panel shows phantom layers that no longer exist in the document. Additionally, PDF/SVG import is not undoable (no command pushed) so an accidental re-Open silently destroys edited work with no recovery, and Place Image drops the image onto the bottom/background layer where it is invisible behind foreground content.

The core SVG round-trip and PNG export are genuinely solid: Export SVG -> Open SVG reproduced the document byte-for-byte at the model level (identical viewBox, identical full-precision attrs, stable ids vf-1/vf-2, identical text content, no overlay leakage, no drift, zero console errors), and PNG export rendered a clean raster that matches the canvas and correctly clips to the artboard. BUT the Document Setup / artboard feature is completely dead: changing the page size via any preset (A3, Square 100) or explicit numeric input (500x400) does NOTHING - viewBox stays -10 -10 230 317 and the white artboard rect stays 210x297, even on a fresh empty document. The before/after screenshots are pixel-identical. Root cause: ArtboardDialog onApply only calls setDimensions (React state); the Canvas effect recomputes viewBox from computeDocumentBounds() which derives purely from the artboard model, but no code path ever calls updateArtboard() when dimensions change, so bounds never moves. Separately I confirmed a keyboard-focus bug: while a text element is in edit mode, single-letter tool shortcuts (v, p, r) are swallowed as typed characters instead of switching tools - my typed 'RoundTrip!' became 'RoundTrip!vp' because the subsequent v/p tool presses leaked into the text, and the intended pen path was never created.

Coordinate math itself is solid: screenToDoc/docToScreen via the SVG CTM is accurate, the status-bar mm readout is exact (moved cursor to doc 105.0,148.5 and status read X=105.0 Y=148.5), the rulers track real zoom correctly at every level (verified at 4%, 120%, 1571%), and hit-testing a rect's center AND near-corner stays pixel-accurate across 100% -> ~430% zoom and after a space-drag pan (selBoxes=1 every time). Anchored Ctrl+wheel zoom keeps the doc point under the cursor stable (105.00 -> 105.00). BUT the user-facing zoom controls are largely broken: the status-bar +/- buttons are completely dead (no onClick wired in App.tsx), there is NO keyboard zoom, NO fit/100%/reset/actual-size affordance anywhere (View menu only has grid/outline/guides), the displayed zoom percent is a lie at startup (shows 100% while the canvas actually renders at ~120%, and you can never reach a true 100%), and ALL plain mouse-wheel scrolling zooms (the wheel handler ignores ctrlKey), so there is no scroll-to-pan and accidental zoom is the default. The zoom clamp constants are also misinterpreted (documented as %-of-natural but compared against raw px/mm), giving a ~3.5%..1571% range instead of the intended 10%..6400%. So: the engine is good, the chrome around it is half-wired.

Most of this journey is in better shape than the baseline assumed. The eyedropper works correctly (picks stroke/fill/stroke-width and new shapes inherit it), single-click erase works and undoes cleanly, the right-click context menu works correctly (enabled items only when there is a selection; Delete/Bring-to-Front/Flip all function), and ALL six overflow tools are actually functional, not orphaned: pencil draws a path, ellipse draws an ellipse, line draws a line, measure shows a non-destructive dimension overlay, lasso selects elements whose bbox-center falls inside the polygon (verified 2 selected when properly enclosed), and free-transform shows 8 scale handles on a live selection. So baseline finding (3) "orphaned/dead tools" is mostly WRONG for the overflow menu — they are reachable and work.

The serious problem is the ERASER drag undo: dragging across multiple shapes erases them all, but undo throws a DOM exception and restores NOTHING — and redo also does nothing. Three shapes were permanently lost with no recovery path. That is silent data loss in a core editing operation. Secondary issues: the rail mislabels the eraser shortcut as "E" but pressing E activates the ellipse tool (eraser's real shortcut is X); the status-bar "Saved" dot is hardcoded green and never reflects unsaved edits; page-nav arrows are permanently disabled stubs; and selecting an overflow tool gives no active-state indication in the rail.

The app is surprisingly robust under fuzzing: I threw 10 rapid draws, random multi-selects, 6x group/ungroup, full align storm, a copy/paste storm that built 70 elements, a 15-tool switch storm including a tool-switch mid-drag, and 40-deep undo/redo storms at it — and got ZERO crashes, ZERO pageerrors, and only the one already-known font warning in the console. Undo/redo integrity is actually solid (verified granular peel-back of delete/paste/draw commands and clean replay via Ctrl+Shift+Z). Group/ungroup, align, multi-select, and copy/paste all behaved correctly. BUT I found two real data-loss bugs the stress journey is designed to surface. (1) CRITICAL: File > Open PDF... silently wipes the entire current document (all your shapes/layers) and the destruction happens OUTSIDE the command history, so Ctrl+Z cannot recover it — confirmed in source (applyParsedSvg removes all layer elements directly, no command). (2) HIGH: the known stale-selection-after-undo bug is not merely cosmetic — when you undo all the way to an empty canvas, the inspector still shows N SELECTED with phantom selection boxes; pressing Delete on that phantom executes a command which wipes the redo stack, permanently stranding the work you just undid (verified: redo x6 afterward restores nothing). I also confirmed a dead ruler guide-drag feature and that Ctrl+Y is not bound to redo. Two things that LOOKED like bugs were test-coordinate/keybinding artifacts and I ruled them out after drilling: dropped draws (my drag start points landed on the 14px ruler strips, which legitimately own pointer events) and 'redo broken' (I had used Ctrl+Y; redo works with Ctrl+Shift+Z).

confirmedHighSev.title: Frame (top X/Y/W/H/R) readout goes stale after any property edit or nudge — shows wrong coordinates until you re-select
confirmedHighSev.repro: 1. Draw a rect, select it. 2. Edit Position X in the Style panel (or the Frame W input itself, or nudge with arrow keys). 3. The top 'Frame' inputs (data-testid=frame-x/frame-w) do NOT update. Example: after committing frame-w=80 the shape width attr=80 but the frame-w input still shows 61.80; after nudging the rect (shape.x -3.82 -> 1.18) frame-x still shows -3.82. Re-clicking the shape (selection refresh) syncs it.
confirmedHighSev.impact: The Frame block is the prominent top-of-inspector coordinate readout. After essentially every edit (drag-nudge, numeric edit in either panel) it lies about the object position/size until the user re-selects. Two panels (Frame vs Position/Size) simultaneously display contradictory values for the identical attribute.
confirmedHighSev.reasoning: Verified by source and screenshot. ControlBar (the top FRAME readout, /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/src/components/ControlBar.tsx) subscribes ONLY to selection changes at line 104 (subscribeSelection), and never to the command history. By contrast PropertiesPanel.tsx:123 explicitly calls history.subscribe(() => setHistoryTick(...)), so it re-renders on every edit. All edit paths flow through history.execute(): ControlBar's own applyAttr/applyAttrs (lines 108/113-114), PropertiesPanel Style edits, and nudge (src/model/nudge.ts:27). history.execute() only notifies history listeners (commands.ts:40 -> notify at 74), never the selection listeners. ControlBar's only other side effect, refreshOverlay (selection.ts:263), just schedules updateOverlay to rebuild SVG handles and does NOT call active.notify(). Therefore the ControlBar never re-runs getBBox(el) after an edit and shows stale x/y/w/h/r until selection fires again. Re-clicking the shape calls setSelection -> notify (selection.ts:46-49), which re-renders ControlBar and resyncs the value, exactly as the repro describes. The screenshot test/review/shots/exp-properties4-negW.png is conclusive: for the same selected rect (vf-1) at the same instant, the top FRAME bar shows W:50.77 while the STYLE > Size panel shows W:-40.00. The two panels disagree because one subscribes to history and the other does not. Real, reproducible, and the stated root cause is correct.

confirmedHighSev.title: Negative / zero W/H accepted into rect, producing invalid SVG, invisible shape, broken selection overlay, and console errors
confirmedHighSev.repro: 1. Draw a rect, select it. 2. Set W to -40 (Size W input or Frame W). 3. width attribute is written as '-40'; the browser logs an error and the rect vanishes. 4. The selection overlay degenerates into ~3 detached collapsed handle squares stacked on the left. Zero is likewise accepted (width='0'). Huge values (88888) also pass straight through.
confirmedHighSev.impact: User can put the document into an invalid render state with garbage geometry and a broken selection overlay. Invalid attributes can also corrupt downstream export.
confirmedHighSev.reasoning:
Confirmed real and reproducible. Screenshot test/review/shots/exp-properties4-negW.png shows exactly what the finding claims: RECT-1 selected (vf-1), Size W = -40.00 (with H 39.73), the rect itself is invisible on the canvas, and the selection overlay has degenerated into ~3 detached collapsed handle squares stacked vertically on the left (~x=148). The Frame W is simultaneously stale at 50.77 while Size W reads -40.00, confirming the overlay/frame desync.

Root cause verified in src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx: 'width' and 'height' are in NUMERIC_ATTRS (line 20), and the only validation in applyAttr is the NaN guard at line 127 (`if (NUMERIC_ATTRS.has(attr) && isNaN(parseFloat(value))) return`). There is no lower-bound clamp to >= 0. The W input onChange (lines 326-341) calls applyAttr(el,'width',v) directly, so parseFloat('-40') = -40 (not NaN) passes through and is written via ModifyAttributeCommand. SVG <rect> rejects negative width per spec, so the browser logs "<rect> attribute width: A negative value is not valid" and refuses to render -> invisible shape; refreshOverlay() at line 340 then reads degenerate geometry -> broken handles. Zero (parseFloat('0')=0) and huge values (88888) likewise pass unchecked. All claimed evidence matches the code.

Severity adjusted down from high to medium: this is a real input-validation gap with degraded UX (invisible shape, broken overlay, console error), but it requires deliberately entering an invalid/nonsensical value, is recoverable via undo or re-entering a positive value, and does not crash the app or irrecoverably corrupt the document. Same gap also affects height and other shapes' size inputs (ellipse rx/ry) that route through applyAttr.

confirmedHighSev.title: Layer hide/lock are not undoable; Ctrl+Z after hide reverts the previous edit and silently deletes drawn content
confirmedHighSev.repro: 1. Draw a rect (it lands in Layer 1, auto-selected). 2. In the Layers panel click the visibility (◉) toggle on Layer 1 to hide it. 3. Press Ctrl+Z expecting to un-hide the layer. RESULT: the layer stays hidden (display:none) and instead the rect's AddElement command is undone (g[data-layer-name] kids 1 -> 0) — the shape is gone. A second Ctrl+Z does nothing, proving hide pushed zero history entries. Same for lock: lock a layer, Ctrl+Z, it stays locked.
confirmedHighSev.impact: Data loss against the user's mental model: a user toggles layer visibility, then hits undo (a reflex), and loses the last shape they drew while the visibility change persists. Visibility and lock are core layer operations and are completely outside the history system.
confirmedHighSev.reasoning:
Confirmed against source and screenshots. In /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/src/components/LayersPanel.tsx, toggleVisibility (lines 105-109) and toggleLock (lines 111-116) mutate the DOM directly (el.style.display, setAttribute/removeAttribute 'data-locked') and call refreshLayers() but NEVER call editor.history.execute(). Contrast with addLayer/deleteLayer/moveLayerUp/moveLayerDown which all push commands via editor.history.execute(). So hide and lock push zero history entries — they are not undoable. This matches the claimed 'C: after lock locked:true; C: after undo still locked:true' and the second Ctrl+Z being a no-op.

The data-loss mechanism is sound: drawing the rect pushes an AddElementCommand onto the undo stack. Hiding the layer adds no history entry, so the next Ctrl+Z pops that AddElementCommand and runs its undo() (commands.ts line 106-110: this.doc.removeElement(this.element)), deleting the rect. The display:none is never reverted, so the layer stays hidden. This exactly matches the claimed probe: 'display:none, kids 1->0'.

Screenshots corroborate: exp-layers-pages-c-B-undo.png shows 'RECT - 1 SELECTED' (vf-1) with a dashed selection box still rendered while the inspector/selection state is stale; exp-layers-pages-05-after-undo-hide.png shows the selection box with three layers present. The persistent selection box despite a removed element is consistent with undo not clearing selection state.

Note: the content is recoverable via redo (AddElementCommand retains the element reference and re-appends it), so it is not strictly permanent loss — but from the user's perspective, hiding a layer then pressing undo silently destroys the visible shape while the panel still shows the layer hidden and a stale 'SELECTED' inspector, with no indication redo would help. Undo hijacking and apparent silent data loss on a completely natural action keeps this at high severity.

confirmedHighSev.title: Hiding a layer leaves a live selection box and 'RECT · 1 SELECTED' inspector on the now-invisible element
confirmedHighSev.repro: 1. Draw a rect (auto-selected). 2. Click the visibility toggle on its layer to hide it. RESULT: the rect's fill vanishes from the canvas but the dashed selection box with all 8 scale handles still renders in place, and the inspector header still reads 'RECT · 1 SELECTED' with fully editable X/Y/W/H frame values (X 35.91, W 26.49).
confirmedHighSev.impact: You can select, drag, resize and edit a shape you cannot see (it's on a hidden layer). Overlay shows phantom geometry; edits land invisibly. This is the same selection-not-cleared family as the owner's confirmed bug #1, triggered by the hide path. toggleVisibility() in LayersPanel mutates style.display without clearing or re-validating selection.
confirmedHighSev.reasoning: Confirmed by both screenshots and source. The two PNGs (test/review/shots/exp-layers-pages-c-A-hidden-selected.png and exp-layers-pages-04-hidden.png) both show the rect's fill gone but the dashed blue selection box with all 8 scale handles still drawn at the rect's location, and the inspector header reading "RECT · 1 SELECTED" with editable Frame X 35.91 / Y 16.49 / W 26.49 / H 22.07. Root cause is in /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/src/components/LayersPanel.tsx toggleVisibility (lines 105-109): it only sets el.style.display = 'none' on the layer <g> and calls refreshLayers(); it never calls clearSelection() (or removes the now-hidden element's descendants from selection) nor refreshOverlaySync() from src/model/selection.ts. The selection state in selection.ts still holds the rect, so the inspector keeps rendering it as selected/editable, and because the overlay group is never rebuilt on hide, the previously-drawn selection box and handles persist on screen even though their target is display:none. The selection-to-layers subscription (subscribeSelection(refreshLayers)) only flows the other direction and does not address this. So a user can still see and edit (X/Y/W/H) an invisible element, which is confusing and inconsistent. It is recoverable (clicking elsewhere clears selection) and causes no crash or data corruption, so it is a stale-UI-state usability defect rather than a critical one. Adjusting from high to medium.

confirmedHighSev.title: Pasting/duplicating a group produces duplicate element IDs (group children keep original IDs) — corrupts exported SVG
confirmedHighSev.repro: 1. Rect tool (R): draw two rects. 2. Select tool (V), marquee-select both. 3. Ctrl+G to group (group=vf-8, children vf-9, vf-10). 4. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V. 5. New group gets fresh id vf-12, but its two child rects are re-inserted with the ORIGINAL ids vf-9 and vf-10. Live DOM now has vf-9 and vf-10 twice. 6. When sibling rects A,B,C are erased left-to-right, A's captured nextSibling is B and B's is C — but B and C are themselves removed. On undo (lines 103-113) elements are re-inserted in original order [A,B,C], so the very first restore calls pos.parent.insertBefore(A, B) while B is still detached, which throws exactly the reported DOMException 'Failed to execute insertBefore on Node: The node before which the new node is to be inserted is not a child of this node.' The single-click case works because it restores exactly one element whose nextSibling was never detached, and other commands (RemoveElementCommand undo, GroupCommand) avoid this by restoring in reverse order or using the live anchor.
