Observe the inspector shows BOTH a top 'Frame' section (X/Y/W/H/R from ControlBar) and, below in Style, a 'Position' (X/Y) + 'Size' (W/H) set from PropertiesPanel. They map to the same x/y/width/height attributes but are two separate input sets that can show different numbers.
allFindings.evidence: Screenshot exp-properties-03-arrow-while-focused shows Frame X:-8.23 at top and Position X:300.00 below for the same selected rect at the same moment. InspectorPanel.tsx:98-103 renders <ControlBar/> under Section 'Frame' AND <PropertiesPanel embedded/> (with its own Position/Size) under Section 'Style'. Rotation is similarly duplicated: Frame R and Transform Rot.
allFindings.impact: Redundant, screen-wasting, and actively misleading when the two diverge. A staff reviewer would flag two overlapping coordinate editors as a design smell.

allFindings.title: Dash 'Custom...' menu option is a dead no-op; no way to enter a custom pattern from a preset
allFindings.repro: 1. Select a rect with a preset (or solid) dash. 2. Open the Dash dropdown and choose 'Custom...'. Nothing happens — the dasharray is unchanged and no input appears.
allFindings.evidence: exp-properties4 stdout: 'dash __custom__ -> dash= 2 2 (custom is a no-op return)'. PropertiesPanel.tsx:614 onChange does `if (e.target.value === '__custom__') return`, and the 'Pat' custom-pattern input (line 635) only renders when the CURRENT dasharray is already a non-preset truthy value — unreachable from a preset/solid state.
allFindings.impact: Misleading menu entry that does nothing. A user wanting a custom dash has no path to it unless a custom value already exists (e.g. from import).

allFindings.title: Layer hide/lock are not undoable; Ctrl+Z after hide reverts the previous edit and silently deletes drawn content
allFindings.repro: 1. Draw a rect (it lands in Layer 1, auto-selected). 2. In the Layers panel click the visibility (◉) toggle on Layer 1 to hide it. 3. Press Ctrl+Z expecting to un-hide the layer. RESULT: the layer stays hidden (display:none) and instead the rect's AddElement command is undone (g[data-layer-name] kids 1 -> 0) — the shape is gone. A second Ctrl+Z does nothing, proving hide pushed zero history entries. Same for lock: lock a layer, Ctrl+Z, it stays locked.
allFindings.evidence: Confirm run: 'A: after HIDE' -> {display:"none", kids:1, selBoxes:1}; 'B: after 1x undo' -> {display:"none", kids:0, selBoxes:1, selLine:"RECT · 1 SELECTED"}; 'B: after 2x undo' identical (history exhausted). 'C: after lock' locked:"true"; 'C: after undo' still locked:"true". Screenshot test/review/shots/exp-layers-pages-c-B-undo.png and exp-layers-pages-05-after-undo-hide.png.
allFindings.impact: Data loss against the user's mental model: a user toggles layer visibility, then hits undo (a reflex), and loses the last shape they drew while the visibility change persists. Visibility and lock are core layer operations and are completely outside the history system.

allFindings.title: Hiding a layer leaves a live selection box and 'RECT · 1 SELECTED' inspector on the now-invisible element
allFindings.repro: 1. Draw a rect (auto-selected). 2. Click the visibility toggle on its layer to hide it. RESULT: the rect's fill vanishes from the canvas but the dashed selection box with all 8 scale handles still renders in place, and the inspector header still reads 'RECT · 1 SELECTED' with fully editable X/Y/W/H frame values (X 35.91, W 26.49).
allFindings.evidence: Confirm run 'A: after HIDE selected element layer' -> {layers:[{display:"none",kids:1}], selBoxes:1, selLine:"RECT · 1 SELECTED"}. Visual: test/review/shots/exp-layers-pages-c-A-hidden-selected.png (no fill drawn, but dashed box + 8 handles visible; inspector shows RECT·1 SELECTED + editable Size/Position). Also exp-layers-pages-04-hidden.png.
allFindings.impact: You can select, drag, resize and edit a shape you cannot see (it's on a hidden layer). Overlay shows phantom geometry; edits land invisibly. This is the same selection-not-cleared family as the owner's confirmed bug #1, triggered by the hide path. toggleVisibility() in LayersPanel mutates style.display without clearing or re-validating selection.

allFindings.title: Multi-page is unimplemented: page-nav is a disabled 'Page 1 / 1' stub and the Inspector 'Pages' tab is a placeholder
allFindings.repro: 1. Look at the status bar: [data-role="page-nav"] shows '◂ Page 1 / 1 ▸' with both arrow buttons rendered disabled (hardcoded). 2. In the Inspector click the 'Pages' tab ([data-role="inspector-properties-tab"]). RESULT: panel body reads 'Multi-page support lands with vectorfeld-4w7.' There is no add-page, navigate, or delete-page control anywhere.
allFindings.evidence: Run output: 'page-nav statusbar' -> '◂ / Page 1 / 1 / ▸'; 'Pages tab content' -> 'Multi-page support lands with vectorfeld-4w7.'. Source: src/components/StatusBar.tsx:84-88 hardcodes '<button disabled>◂</button> Page 1 / 1 <button disabled>▸</button>'. src/components/InspectorPanel.tsx:135-139 renders the placeholder string for bottomTab==='properties'. Screenshot test/review/shots/exp-layers-pages-09-pages-tab.png.
allFindings.impact: The 'multi-page add/nav/delete' half of this journey does not exist in the UI. Per-page element isolation cannot be tested. Note the Inspector tab is labelled 'Pages' but its data-role is 'inspector-properties-tab', a confusing naming mismatch.

allFindings.title: No way to rename a layer; names are auto-assigned only
allFindings.repro: Add several layers. Try to rename one: double-click the name span, single-click-to-edit, or look for a rename input/context menu. RESULT: nothing. The name span is plain text with no edit handler; rows only expose visibility, lock, up, down and delete buttons.
allFindings.evidence: layerRows() output shows each row has 4-5 buttons (vis/lock/up/down[/delete]) and a static name span. LayersPanel.tsx renders {layer.name} at lines 227-237 with no onDoubleClick / editing state anywhere in the file. Names only ever come from addLayer's `Layer ${n}` default or the imported data-layer-name.
allFindings.impact: 'rename' is an explicit requirement of this journey and is not implementable through the UI. Users are stuck with 'Layer 1/2/3' and imported names.

allFindings.title: Deleting the active layer leaves activeLayerIdx pointing at a stale/wrong row (off-by-one risk)
allFindings.repro: Add 3 layers. Delete a middle layer via its × button. The deleteLayer handler computes the new active index from the OLD layers array length, not the post-delete state: `if (activeLayerIdx >= layers.length - 1) setActiveLayerIdx(Math.max(0, layers.length - 2))`. After delete, refreshLayers() shrinks the list but the active-row highlight can land on a different layer than the one the user was working in, and the effect that calls setActiveLayerElement() then re-points the active drawing target.
allFindings.evidence: Source LayersPanel.tsx:97-103 (deleteLayer) reads stale `layers.length` and `activeLayerIdx` captured in the closure; the index math runs against pre-delete length. In the drive run, after deleting down to the last layer the surviving layer was 'Layer 3' (the previously-active one) rather than 'Layer 1', confirming the active-pointer follows non-obvious rules. No crash, but the active layer can silently change.
allFindings.impact: Subsequent draws can land in an unexpected layer after a delete; the highlighted 'active' row may not match the real active drawing target. Low because no data loss and no error, but it is an interlock/state-correctness smell.

allFindings.title: Pasting/duplicating a group produces duplicate element IDs (group children keep original IDs) — corrupts exported SVG
allFindings.repro: 1. Rect tool (R): draw two rects. 2. Select tool (V), marquee-select both. 3. Ctrl+G to group (group=vf-8, children vf-9, vf-10). 4. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V. 5. New group gets fresh id vf-12, but its two child rects are re-inserted with the ORIGINAL ids vf-9 and vf-10. Live DOM now has vf-9 and vf-10 twice. 6. File > Export SVG: the exported file contains id="vf-9" twice and id="vf-10" twice. Same path via Ctrl+D (duplicateSelection) since it calls pasteClipboard.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario stdout: 'STEP7 DUPLICATE IDS: ["vf-9","vf-10"]'. Exported SVG id histogram (grep): '2 id="vf-9" / 2 id="vf-10"'. Raw block: <g id="vf-12" transform="matrix(1,0,0,1,5,5)"><rect id="vf-9" .../><rect id="vf-10" .../></g> duplicating the original group vf-8's children. Screenshots: /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/test/review/shots/exp-clipboard-09-group-pasted.png , /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/test/review/shots/exp-clipboard-export.svg
allFindings.impact: Duplicate IDs in exported SVG are invalid (id must be unique per document). Downstream consumers (browsers, getElementById, CSS #id selectors, other editors, re-import) bind to the first match only, so the second copy's children become unaddressable / can mis-render or break url(#...) references (gradients, clip-paths, masks defined inside a copied group would all collide). Internally, selection/lookup by id can target the wrong element. This is silent data corruption that scales: each paste of an N-child group adds N more colliding ids.

allFindings.title: Artboard id 'ab-1' appears as a duplicate id in exported SVG (artboard rect + layer group)
allFindings.repro: Export any document to SVG (File > Export SVG) and grep for id=. The artboard id 'ab-1' is emitted as both data-artboard-id and as id on multiple nodes; histogram shows id="ab-1" twice.
allFindings.evidence: grep of /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/test/review/shots/exp-clipboard-export.svg: '2 id="ab-1"'. Nodes: <rect ... data-role="artboard" data-artboard-id="ab-1"/> and <g data-layer-name="Layer 1" data-artboard-id="ab-1" ...>. Pre-existing (not clipboard-caused) but surfaces in the same duplicate-id check.
allFindings.impact: Another duplicate-id source in exported SVG; minor because these are structural/data attributes, but combined with the group bug it means exports are reliably non-unique-id. Worth fixing alongside id hygiene.

allFindings.title: Pen tool cannot create asymmetric/cusp handles — Alt is completely ignored, handles always force-mirrored
allFindings.repro: 1) Press P. 2) Click at canvas (300,300). 3) Click-drag at (450,350) holding Alt, dragging the handle straight right to (510,350). 4) Inspect the preview path d-string. Result: the dragged anchor's handleIn is the exact mirror of where the drag pulled (handleOut), regardless of Alt. There is no key/modifier that produces an independent (asymmetric) outgoing vs incoming handle, so corners/cusps are impossible to author with the pen.
allFindings.evidence: Instrumented test recorded altKey on every drag mousemove as true: 'altKey on drag moves: [false,true,true,true,true,true,true,true,true,true,true]'. Yet resulting preview D = 'M 35.91 38.56 C 35.91 38.56 55.777 49.597 69.021 49.597' — for anchor (69.02,49.6) the incoming handle (55.777,49.597) is exactly mirror-symmetric. Also confirmed on the interior anchor of the committed S-curve path: anchor (69.021,49.597) had handleIn rel (-13.244,-8.829) and handleOut rel (+13.244,+8.829) — perfect mirror. Source penTool.ts onMouseMove lines 299-305 sets anchor.handleOut={pt} and anchor.handleIn={2*pos-pt} with no altKey branch anywhere in the file.
allFindings.impact: You cannot draw cusps, corners with one straight + one curved side, or any asymmetric bezier with the pen. Every node is forced smooth/symmetric. Authoring real vector art requires asymmetric handles; the only workaround is to draw symmetric then re-edit each side in Direct Select, which is tedious and non-discoverable. This is a core feature gap for a vector editor.

allFindings.title: Pen/export never emits S/s smooth bezier shorthand — only verbose C commands, smooth continuity not encoded
allFindings.repro: 1) Press P. 2) Draw a 3-anchor S-curve by click-dragging a handle at each anchor (e.g. (300,300) drag +60,-40; (450,350) drag +60,+40; (600,300) drag +60,-40). 3) Enter to finish. 4) File > Export SVG and inspect the path d. Result: the d-string is entirely 'M ... C ... C ...' — zero S/s commands, even though consecutive segments are smooth (mirrored handles) and S/s would be the natural compact encoding.
allFindings.evidence: Exported SVG d-string [3]: 'M 35.91 38.56 C 62.40 20.90 55.78 40.77 69.02 49.60 C 82.26 58.43 88.89 47.39 102.13 38.56 C 115.37 29.73 113.17 38.56 124.20 49.60'. Test regex 'Has S/s smooth command anywhere? false'. Source: buildPathD in penTool.ts (lines 53-68) only ever appends ' C ...'; parsePathWithHandles/updatePathControlPoint in directSelectTool.ts only handle M/L/C/Z (regex [MLCZmlcz]) — S/s aren't produced or parsed.
allFindings.impact: Output is geometrically correct so rendering looks fine, but: (a) d-strings are more verbose than necessary; (b) the smooth/continuity relationship between adjacent segments is not expressed (no S), so downstream tools or re-imports treat every node's two handles as fully independent rather than smooth, and round-tripping cannot recover the authored 'smooth' intent. For a vector editor that advertises bezier S-curves this is a real fidelity/encoding gap.

allFindings.title: Select-tool bounding box on a finished path persists after switching to Direct Select on another path
allFindings.repro: 1) Draw and close a path with the pen (it auto-selects the new path and switches to the Select tool, drawing a scale-handle bounding box). 2) Press A (Direct Select) and click a DIFFERENT path. Result: the new path shows direct-select anchors, but the previously-selected closed path still renders the select-tool dashed bounding box with 8 scale handles simultaneously.
allFindings.evidence: Shots exp-pen-bezier-09-anchor-selected.png and exp-pen-bezier-10-handle-dragged.png both show the lower (closed) path wrapped in a blue dashed select-box with corner/edge handles while the upper (open) path is in direct-select anchor-edit mode. penTool.finish() calls setSelection([el]) + setActiveTool('select') (lines 187), and that selection/overlay is not cleared when direct-select takes over.
allFindings.impact: Cosmetic/confusing: two different selection paradigms shown at once. No data loss, but it muddies which element is being edited and overlaps with baseline bug (1) about selection state not being cleared on tool/state transitions.

allFindings.title: Corner scale handles are overlapped by invisible rotation zones; clicking the handle center/outer-half rotates instead of scaling
allFindings.repro: 1) Draw a rect (R), switch to Select (V), click it. 2) Move mouse to the visual center of any corner handle (e.g. SE bottom-right white square) and drag outward. Instead of resizing, the shape gets a rotate() transform and width/height stay unchanged. Dragging from a point ~3px INSIDE the handle (toward the shape) does scale. Verified with elementFromPoint at 5 offsets across the SE handle: dead-center=>rotation-handle=>ROTATE (w 35.32 unchanged), inner(-3,-3)=>scale-handle=>SCALE (w 35.32->47.9), outer(+3,+3)=>ROTATE, (+4,+4)=>ROTATE, (-4,-4)=>SCALE.
allFindings.evidence: selection.ts renders 8 scale handles (10px, centered on corner at [cx-5,cx+5]) then appends 4 rotation 'zone' rects of size hs*2=20px. For SE the zone is at x=cx,y=cy (offX/offY=0) spanning [cx,cx+20]x[cy,cy+20], i.e. it covers the corner-facing half AND the exact center of the SE scale handle; appended last it wins SVG hit-testing. Same pattern all 4 corners. Probe: 'click@(360.0,320.0) elementFromPoint={role:rotation-handle} => before w=35.32 after w=35.32 t=rotate(-0.0000026...)' => MODE=ROTATE.
allFindings.impact: Core resize gesture is unreliable: users aiming at the corner handle frequently rotate the shape by a tiny amount (e.g. rotate(-0.138...)) instead of scaling, silently corrupting the transform and producing no visible resize. This is the actual reason on-canvas corner-scale 'looks broken'.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/src/model/selection.ts (lines 208-258: scale handles 10px centered on corner; rotation zones hs*2=20px appended after, overlapping the corner-facing half + center of each scale handle)

allFindings.title: Baseline finding (4) 'no rotation handle on canvas' is inaccurate — rotation IS on canvas but as hidden corner zones that conflict with scaling
allFindings.repro: Select a single shape; the 4 corner regions over/just-outside each corner handle act as rotation affordances (rotHandles=4 in DOM, custom rotate cursors). They are transparent (fill:transparent) so not visually discoverable, and they overlap the scale handles (see exp-transform-1).
allFindings.evidence: DOM after selecting one rect: {selBoxes:1, scaleHandles:8, rotHandles:4}. selection.ts assigns ROTATION_CURSORS and data-role='rotation-handle' to 4 transparent corner rects when selectedElements.length===1.
allFindings.impact: The previously-reported 'rotation only via numeric field' is wrong; canvas rotation exists but is undiscoverable (invisible) and steals scale clicks. Fixing exp-transform-1 should also make rotation visible/distinct (offset the rotation ring outward beyond the handle, or shrink the zone so it never covers the handle center).

allFindings.title: Non-uniform drag-scale of a heavily-rotated shape collapses one axis with no constraint feedback
allFindings.repro: 1) Draw a rect, rotate it ~97deg (on-canvas or numeric Rot). 2) Drag a corner scale handle (inner part, to avoid the rotation-zone bug) diagonally without Shift. Result: width 33.11->42.21 but height 19.87->3.27 — the shape becomes a thin sliver for a modest +70,+50px diagonal drag.
allFindings.evidence: Captured: beforeScaleRot {w:33.11,h:19.87,transform:rotate(96.9...)} -> afterScaleRot {w:42.21,h:3.27,same transform}. Screenshot exp-transform-06 shows a thin parallelogram. With Shift (uniform) on a 45deg square the result is correct (aspect w/h=1.000, 30.9->45.4 both axes), proving the local-space inverse-transform math is right; the sliver is the legitimate local-axis mapping of a diagonal screen drag onto a rotated frame.
allFindings.impact: Geometrically defensible but confusing UX: free corner-scaling of a rotated object yields wild aspect distortion with no live numeric/visual hint of which local axis is moving. Users will perceive it as a bug. Consider screen-aligned scaling for rotated shapes, or live W/H during the drag.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/src/tools/selectTool.ts (onMouseMove scale branch, lines 583-624: inverse-transforms mouse to local space and scales local attrs; correct but unconstrained)

allFindings.title: VERIFIED-WORKING: numeric rotate preserves skew; SkX/SkY emit real skew; uniform scale of rotated shapes correct; multi-select group scale correct
allFindings.repro: Skew probe (typed with focus+Enter): Rot=0 then SkX=30 => 'skewX(30)'; SkY=20 => 'skewX(30) skewY(20)'; Rot=15 => 'rotate(15, cx, cy) skewX(30) skewY(20)' (skew preserved). Uniform Shift-scale of 45deg square: aspect w/h=1.000, 30.9->45.4. Multi-select 3 rects + SE drag: all grow 17.66->24.02 and gaps grow, anchored at NW.
allFindings.evidence: exp-transform-skew and exp-transform-rotscale probe outputs (aspect 1.000). Multi: before bboxes [w17.66 x3] -> after [w24.02 x3]. An initial automated run mis-reported SkX as writing rotate() — that was the test helper hitting the wrong input without focusing; re-test with proper focus disproved it.
allFindings.impact: Positive: the transform model (matrix.ts setSkew/parseSkew/scaleAroundMatrix, selectTool local-space scaling, handleTransform on the overlay) is solid. Do not rewrite it; only fix the handle-overlap interaction.

allFindings.title: Ungroup silently discards the group's transform, moving every child (data corruption)
allFindings.repro: See evidence; reproduced in test/review/scenarios/exp-align-zorder-3.mjs
allFindings.evidence: Scenario exp-align-zorder-3.mjs applied transform='translate(40,40) rotate(15)' to the group, then ungrouped. Children screen positions WITH group transform: vf-2(476,349) vf-1(282,297) vf-3(669,400). AFTER ungroup: vf-2(320,120) vf-1(120,120) vf-3(520,120), each with transform='' (empty). Logged drift per child: vf-2 dx=-156 dy=-229, vf-1 dx=-162 dy=-177, vf-3 dx=-149 dy=-280 — should be ~0 if transform were preserved. Screenshot exp-align-zorder-3-grp-ungrouped.png shows the rects snapped back to axis-aligned top-left, no longer rotated. UngroupCommand.execute() (src/model/commands.ts:271-277) just does parent.insertBefore(child, group) and removes the group without baking the group's transform matrix into each child.
allFindings.impact: Any ungroup of a transformed group corrupts the document: shapes teleport and de-rotate. Because grouping then moving a group is a normal workflow, this loses user work silently with no warning and no error.

allFindings.title: Selection overlay and inspector ignore an ancestor group's transform
allFindings.repro: 1. Create 3 rects, group them. 2. Apply transform='translate(40,40) rotate(15)' to the group. 3. Select the group. Observe selection box vs actual shapes, and the inspector Rot field.
allFindings.evidence: Screenshot exp-align-zorder-3-grp-transformed.png: the dashed selection box sits in the TOP-LEFT corner while the three actual (rotated, translated) rects are mid-canvas — the overlay is fully detached from the rendered geometry. Inspector shows Rot: 0.00 despite the group carrying rotate(15). The overlay computes bounds from the element's own coords without composing ancestor transforms.
allFindings.impact: Once a group has any transform, you cannot reliably select/scale/rotate it on canvas — the handles are in the wrong place and the inspector lies about rotation. Compounds the ungroup bug: users can't even tell the group is transformed.

allFindings.title: Grouping reorders children by selection (click) order, corrupting z-order
allFindings.repro: 1. Create 3 overlapping rects in DOM order vf-1 (back), vf-2 (front), vf-3. 2. Shift-click them in a different order, e.g. vf-3, then vf-1, then vf-2. 3. Object > Group. Inspect the group's child order.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario exp-align-zorder-8.mjs: DOM order before = vf-1,vf-2,vf-3. After selecting in order vf-3,vf-1,vf-2 and grouping, the group's children are vf-3,vf-1,vf-2 — selection order, NOT document/z-order. GroupCommand (src/model/commands.ts:230-242) stores this.children=[...children] in selection order, appends them in that order, and inserts the group at children[0] (the first-CLICKED element). addToSelection (src/model/selection.ts:52-54) pushes in click order. Because vf-1/vf-2 overlap, their stacking flips on group (vf-2 was in front of vf-1; after group vf-1 is in front).
allFindings.impact: Grouping visibly changes the rendered stacking whenever the user's click order differs from document order — which is common. Group should be a no-op for appearance; here it silently restacks overlapping shapes.

allFindings.title: Plain click on an already-selected element does not collapse a multi-selection to one
allFindings.repro: 1. Create 3 shapes. 2. Select all (Ctrl+A, or shift-click each). 3. Single plain click (no drag) on one of the selected shapes. Expected: selection collapses to just that shape. Actual: stays multi-selected.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario exp-align-zorder-6.mjs: built a real 3-selection via shift-click (verified 3 selection boxes), then plain-clicked shape A: selection boxes stayed at 3 (expected 1). Same after Ctrl+A then plain-click B: stayed 3. Screenshot exp-align-zorder-6-collapse.png. Root cause: selectTool onMouseDown (src/tools/selectTool.ts:499-503) keeps the existing selection if the clicked element is already in it (to allow group-drag); onMouseUp's no-drag dead-zone branch (selectTool.ts:720-752) just cleans up and returns with NO collapse-to-clicked-element logic.
allFindings.impact: You cannot drill from a multi-selection down to a single element by clicking — a core interaction. This directly breaks the align/z-order journey: after Ctrl+A a user clicking one shape still has all selected, so Object>Bring-to-Front etc. silently no-op (z-order requires sel.length===1), giving a confusing dead-end. Verified separately that z-order menu items are enabled at selCount>0 but bringToFront/etc. in src/model/zOrder.ts early-return unless exactly 1 is selected.

allFindings.title: Z-order menu items are enabled for multi-selection but silently do nothing
allFindings.repro: 1. Create 3 shapes, select all (Ctrl+A). 2. Object > Bring to Front (also Bring Forward / Send Backward / Send to Back). Observe DOM order unchanged.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario exp-align-zorder.mjs: 'Multi Bring to Front before: vf-1,vf-2,vf-3 / after: vf-1,vf-2,vf-3 / changed? false'. The Object menu enables these items whenever selCount!==0 (src/App.tsx:196-199 use disabled: selCount === 0), but bringToFront/bringForward/sendBackward/sendToBack (src/model/zOrder.ts:11-50) all `if (sel.length !== 1) return`. So with 2+ selected the command is a clickable no-op with no feedback.
allFindings.impact: Confusing dead control: users multi-select and try to restack, nothing happens, no error. Either the items should be disabled for multi-select or z-order should handle multiple elements.

allFindings.title: Distribute Horizontal/Vertical are absent from the Object menu (only in Inspector)
allFindings.repro: 1. Select 3+ shapes. 2. Open Object menu. There are 6 Align items but no Distribute items. Distribute H/V exist only as 'H'/'V' buttons in the Inspector panel.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario exp-align-zorder.mjs scanned the open Object menu for /distribute/i buttons and found []. src/App.tsx Object menu (lines 201-224) maps only the 6 AlignOps, no computeDistribute wiring. Distribute itself works: exp-align-zorder-7.mjs clicked the Inspector 'H' button and centers went from 3,25,100 to evenly-spaced 3,51,100 (gaps 48/49).
allFindings.impact: Discoverability gap and menu/inspector inconsistency — Align is in both places, Distribute only in the Inspector. Functionally fine once found.

allFindings.title: Stale selection persists after undo: 3 phantom selection boxes + 8 handles + "3 SELECTED" inspector float over a fully empty canvas
allFindings.repro: 1. Rect tool (R), draw 3 rects. 2. Select tool (V), Ctrl+A (selBox=3, inspector "3 SELECTED / 3 items"). 3. Press Ctrl+Z three times to undo every rect away. RESULT: canvas is completely empty (no fills, kids=0) but 3 dashed selection-boxes, 8 scale-handles, and the full inspector panel ("3 SELECTED / 3 items / FRAME 3 objects / Align / Distribute") remain rendered. Even one single undo (kids=2) leaves selBox=3 — the removed rect keeps its phantom box immediately.
allFindings.evidence: test/review/scenarios/exp-undo-redo-2.mjs output: "A after 1 undo (rect3 removed, was selected): kids=2 selBox=3 handles=8 insp=\"3 SELECTED 3 items...\"" and "A undo-to-empty: kids=0 selBox=3 handles=8 insp=\"3 SELECTED 3 items...\"". Screenshot shows blank artboard with 3 dashed boxes + handles + populated Align/Distribute panel.
allFindings.impact: User is shown a UI that claims 3 objects are selected over a blank document. Every selection-dependent control (Align, Distribute, nudge, group, style edits) is live and clickable against geometry that no longer exists. Erodes trust and is the gateway to the data-resurrection bug below.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: src/model/commands.ts (CommandHistory.undo/redo lines 43-57 never touch selection) + src/model/selection.ts (selected[] holds raw detached Element refs; updateOverlay draws boxes via getBBox which still succeeds on detached nodes, lines 146-178) + src/model/EditorContext.tsx (lines 118,121 call history.undo()/redo() with no clearSelection/prune)

allFindings.title: Data resurrection: Ctrl+D on a phantom (post-undo) selection clones the deleted element back into the live document
allFindings.repro: 1. Rect tool (R), draw one rect. 2. Select tool (V), click it (selBox=1, "RECT 1 SELECTED vf-4"). 3. Ctrl+Z once -> rect removed, canvas empty (kids=0) but phantom selBox=1 / "RECT 1 SELECTED vf-4" remains. 4. Press Ctrl+D (Duplicate). RESULT: a real new rect vf-5 appears on the empty canvas (kids=1), fully styled, selected, inspector shows X/Y/W/H. The document is now dirty with geometry the user never re-created.
allFindings.evidence: exp-undo-redo-3.mjs output: "phantom-1 after undo: kids=0 selBox=1 insp=\"RECT 1 SELECTED vf-4...\"" then "after Ctrl+D on phantom: kids=1 selBox=1 insp=\"RECT 1 SELECTED vf-5...\"". Screenshot exp-undo-redo-phantom-dup.png shows a real rect on a canvas that undo had emptied. Root cause read: duplicateSelection() in src/model/clipboard.ts:102-107 does getSelection() (returns detached vf-4), copySelection() serializes it, pasteClipboard() inserts the clone — no isConnected/parentElement guard anywhere.
allFindings.impact: Silent injection of ghost geometry into a document the user believed they had emptied via undo. The resurrected element is a normal node that exports straight into the PDF/SVG. A user who undoes a delete and then duplicates (a very common motion) gets a stray object they did not author. Corrupts WYSIWYG and the exported artifact.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: src/model/clipboard.ts:102 duplicateSelection -> getSelection() returns stale detached refs with no live-node filter; underlying cause is the unreconciled selection from finding 01.

allFindings.title: Silent no-op on phantom selection: nudge / Align / Group execute against detached nodes and do nothing while UI claims a selection exists
allFindings.repro: After reaching the phantom state (3 rects, Ctrl+A, undo to empty; kids=0 selBox=3 "3 SELECTED"): (a) press ArrowRight -> nothing moves (no element to nudge), selBox stays 3. (b) Click Align L in inspector -> no-op, kids stays 0, no crash. (c) Press Ctrl+G -> no-op, kids stays 0. In every case the inspector/overlay keep insisting 3 objects are selected.
allFindings.evidence: exp-undo-redo-2.mjs: "A phantom-nudge: selBox 3->3, kids 0->0". exp-undo-redo-3.mjs: "after Align L: kids=0 selBox=3" and "after phantom group: kids=0 selBox=3". No console/page errors in any run.
allFindings.impact: Commands silently fail with no feedback. The user clicks Align/nudges expecting an effect on the 3 "selected" objects and nothing happens, with no error or selection clear to explain why. Confusing, but non-destructive (no crash, no corruption) — hence medium not high.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: src/model/EditorContext.tsx (nudge/align/group handlers operate on getSelection() detached refs) and src/model/selection.ts (no pruning); same root cause as finding 01.

allFindings.title: Selection overlay never reconciles even when redo/undo restores or removes the underlying elements
allFindings.repro: From the phantom state, press Ctrl+Shift+Z (redo) repeatedly: elements come back (kids 1->2->3) but selBox stays pinned at 3 the entire time and is never re-derived from the restored nodes. Conversely, after Ctrl+D resurrection, undoing 3x drops kids to 0 but selBox stays 1 throughout.
allFindings.evidence: exp-undo-redo-3.mjs redo loop: "redo#1: kids=1 selBox=3 / redo#2: kids=2 selBox=3 / redo#3: kids=3 selBox=3". exp-undo-redo-4.mjs: "undo#1 after resurrect: kids=0 selBox=1 / undo#2: kids=0 selBox=1 / undo#3: kids=0 selBox=1".
allFindings.impact: The selection overlay is fully decoupled from document state across the whole undo/redo axis, not just at the empty boundary. Even after redo restores the real elements, the displayed selection boxes are stale and may not correspond to what is actually editable. Compounds the confusion of findings 01/03.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: src/model/commands.ts CommandHistory.undo/redo (lines 43-57) emit a notify() for history listeners but never call updateOverlay() or re-validate selection; src/model/selection.ts overlay is only refreshed by selection mutators.

allFindings.title: POSITIVE: document-content undo/redo round-trips byte-identically; branch truncation correct
allFindings.repro: Part B: fresh doc, draw 2 rects, nudge one down 3px, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+G (group). Undo 10x to empty, redo 10x. Compare layer outerHTML peak vs restored. Branch test: build 4 ops, undo 3, draw a new rect, then press redo.
allFindings.evidence: exp-undo-redo-2.mjs: "B STRICT XML MATCH (peak vs redo-all): true" and "B CANON XML MATCH: true". exp-undo-redo.mjs branch test: "BRANCH: redo after new-op changed kids? before=3 afterNewOp+redo=4" (redo was correctly a no-op; the new op truncated the redo stack). Zero console/page/request errors across all four scripts.
allFindings.impact: Confirms the underlying command-stack and document-mutation logic are correct and trustworthy. The bugs above are confined to the SELECTION/overlay layer, which is why the journey is fixable rather than needing rework — the hard part (faithful content undo) already works.

allFindings.title: Escape during rectangle drag is a no-op AND the rect still commits on mouseup (cannot abort a rectangle)
allFindings.repro: Press R (rect tool). On canvas: mouse-down at ~(200,200), drag to ~(320,300) — a preview rect appears. Press Escape (mouse still held). Observe: nothing happens — the preview rect stays, tool stays 'rect', drawing continues. Release mouse. Observe: the rectangle is committed (layerKids 0->1, selBox appears, switches to select tool).
allFindings.evidence: Isolated run B: [B.mid-drag] previews:1 activeTool:rect. After Escape: [B.after-Escape(mouse-down)] previews:1 activeTool:rect (UNCHANGED — Escape ignored). After mouseup: [B.after-mouseup] layerKids:1 selBoxes:1 activeTool:select inspector 'RECT 1 SELECTED'. Screenshot exp-tool-switch-B-escape-during-drag.png shows the preview rect still on canvas with R tool active after Escape. Root cause: src/tools/rectTool.ts has no handlers.onKeyDown, so Canvas's keydown dispatch (src/components/Canvas.tsx:350 getActiveTool()?.handlers.onKeyDown?.(e)) finds nothing and Escape does nothing; state.drawing stays true so the next onMouseUp commits the shape. Compare penTool.ts:377 which handles Escape via cleanup().
allFindings.impact: There is no keyboard way to abort an in-progress rectangle. Users expect Escape to cancel a drag (every other vector editor does, and pen does here). Worse, the abort gesture is silently ignored and the shape gets created anyway on release, producing an unwanted element.

allFindings.title: Inconsistent mid-operation tool-switch policy: rect discards, but pen and text silently COMMIT a half-finished element
allFindings.repro: PEN: Press P, click 3 points on canvas (path not finished), press V. Observe layerKids 0->1 and a path is selected — a partial path was committed. TEXT: Press T, click canvas, type 'HELLO', click the Select tool slot. Observe a 'HELLO' text element is committed. RECT: Press R, mouse-down+drag, press V — the preview is discarded and NOTHING is created (layerKids stays 0).
allFindings.evidence: Run-2 PEN-SWITCH: [mid-pen-3] previews:5 activeTool:pen layerKids:0; [after-V] layerKids:1 selBoxes:1 inspector 'PATH 1 SELECTED'. Run-2 TEXT-COMMIT-ON-SWITCH: [mid-type] activeTool:text; [after-click-select-slot] layerKids:1 inspector 'TEXT 1 SELECTED HELLO'. Run-1 A (rect): [A.after-V-keypress] previews:0 layerKids:0 — discarded. Root cause: penTool.ts:201 onDeactivate(){ if(state.drawing) finish() } and textTool.ts:265 onDeactivate(){ if(state.editing) commit() } COMMIT; rectTool.ts:73 onDeactivate(){ state.drawing=false; removePreview() } DISCARDS.
allFindings.impact: Same gesture (switch tool while drawing) yields opposite outcomes depending on the tool: pen/text leave behind an element the user may not have wanted, rect throws away work. The asymmetry is surprising and means an accidental tool-switch keystroke during pen/text creates stray geometry.

allFindings.title: Tool keyboard shortcuts (r/v/p) cannot switch tools while editing text — they are typed as literal characters into the text
allFindings.repro: Press T, click canvas, type 'AB', press r, press v, press Escape. Observe the committed text is 'ABrv' — the r and v were inserted as text, not interpreted as tool shortcuts.
allFindings.evidence: Run-2 TEXT-SHORTCUT-SWALLOW: [after-AB-then-r-v] activeTool stays 'text'; [after-escape] inspector 'TEXT 1 SELECTED ABrv'. Run-1 also produced 'HELLOrvt'. Screenshot exp-tool-switch-text-swallow.png shows committed text 'ABrv'. Root cause: textTool.startEditing sets setKeyboardCapture(true) (textTool.ts:223), and useToolShortcuts.ts:7 returns early when isKeyboardCaptured(), so shortcut keys never reach setActiveTool and fall through to textTool's printable-char insert (textTool.ts:405-414).
allFindings.impact: While typing text the only ways to leave the text tool are Escape/Enter (which commit) or a mouse click on a tool slot. A muscle-memory tool shortcut silently corrupts the text content. This is partly defensible (you want letters to type), but there is no modifier/Escape-then-shortcut affordance, so it is a real friction point and a data-correctness footgun.

allFindings.title: Inspector shows stale prior selection (RECT properties) after switching to the Text/Pen tool
allFindings.repro: Draw a rectangle (auto-selected). Press T. Observe inspector still reads 'RECT 1 SELECTED' with rect Frame/Style fields and the selection-box overlay is still drawn, even though the active tool is now Text (a creation tool).
allFindings.evidence: Run-3: [rect-made(selected)] inspector 'RECT 1 SELECTED' selBoxes:1; [after-switch-to-text] activeTool:text but inspector still 'RECT 1 SELECTED' selBoxes:1; same after switching to pen and back to rect. Screenshot exp-tool-switch-inspector-after-text-switch.png. setActiveTool (registry.ts:33) only toggles active tool and never touches selection, so selection persists across tool changes.
allFindings.impact: Switching to a creation tool presents the old object's properties rather than a clean creation context, which is confusing. Matches the journey's pre-noted 'inspector keeps showing prior selection after switching to Text tool'. Low severity because the selection genuinely persists (clicking with the new tool replaces it) and no data is lost.

allFindings.title: Imported PDF text content cannot be edited by ANY path (no edit affordance exists)
allFindings.repro: 1) File > Open PDF... > 'Flyer Swift Vortragscoaching 15.04.2026 noheader.pdf'. 2) Select tool (V). 3) Single-click the body line 'Ich entlaste...' — inspector shows 'G · 1 SELECTED' with generic group props, no Font/content field. 4) Double-click the same text — still 'G · 1 SELECTED', no edit mode; type 'ZZZ' -> all 106 text runs unchanged (stillHasOriginal:true). 5) Text tool (T), click over the text, type 'Typo fix' -> a NEW empty text is started; original line unchanged, typed text not committed. There is no 'Edit Text' menu item anywhere.
allFindings.evidence: Probe output: A) singleclick -> {selBoxes:1, hasFontSection:false, inspectorHead:'G · 1 SELECTED | Ich entlaste'}. B) dblclick -> identical 'G · 1 SELECTED', AFTER ZZZ -> {stillHasOriginal:true, totalTexts:106}. C) text-tool-over selected a 'g' (G · 1 SELECTED, generic Position/Transform/Style, no Font), typed text not committed. DOM inventory: layerDirectChildren:112, breakdown {g:112} — every text run is wrapped in its own <g>; the text run's parentTag is 'g' (parentHasLayer:false).
allFindings.impact: The product's stated core use case — editing text in a Word-generated PDF — is completely non-functional. A user cannot fix even a single typo. This makes the editable-PDF value proposition false.
allFindings.consoleError: warning: Font cannot be both symbolic and non-symbolic. Skipping subsetting.

allFindings.title: Hit test selects the wrapping <g>, never the inner <text> — blocks all text-specific UI
allFindings.repro: Open the editable PDF, Select tool, click any text run. hitTestElement (src/model/geometry.ts:186-209) loops only `layer.children` (direct children). PDF import nests each <text> inside its own <g> (src/model/pdfImport.ts flattenAndScalePdfLayer leaves a <g> wrapper per run). So the returned element is the <g>, and PropertiesPanel renders the tag==='g' branch.
allFindings.evidence: hitTestElement iterates `const children = layer.children` and `return child` for the first <g> AABB hit — it never descends. DOM: all 112 layer children are <g>, each containing exactly one <text> (gKids childTags:['text']). PropertiesPanel.tsx:453 `tag === 'text' && (...Font section...)` is therefore never satisfied for imported text.
allFindings.impact: Even if the user wanted to change font/size/letter-spacing of imported text, those controls are unreachable because the selectable element is always a group. This is the structural root cause feeding the recolor and edit failures.

allFindings.title: Recolor (gate-10) of imported text is impossible: fill-type reads 'none', no fill color picker rendered
allFindings.repro: Open editable PDF, Select tool, click the blue heading/body text. Inspector Style section shows Fill dropdown = 'None' and offers NO fill ColorPicker. There is no way to set the text color from the UI.
allFindings.evidence: Inspector inputs enumerated after selecting 'Ich entlaste': only `fill-type` SELECT with value 'none' and a `colorpicker-stroke` BUTTON — `[data-testid="fill"]` count is 0, no input[type=color] in inspector. Before/after fill on the actual <text> is unchanged after attempting recolor; D-recolor export render still shows the original blue (#2f5496) text. detectFillType reads the selected <g> (fill:null) and returns 'none', so the solid-fill ColorPicker branch (PropertiesPanel.tsx ~551 `fillType==='solid'`) never renders.
allFindings.impact: The gate-10 recolor path cannot be exercised by a user on imported PDF text — the most basic styling change is blocked. Combined with PropertiesPanel.tsx:130 distributing g-fill to children, even if a color WERE settable it would write to the group not necessarily the run; but the control is absent entirely.

allFindings.title: Text is fragmented into per-line <g> runs; delete/move operate on fragments, not logical text
allFindings.repro: Open editable PDF, Select tool, click the body line 'Ich entlaste durch mein Lektorat...', press Delete. Only the 'Ich entlaste ' prefix fragment disappears; the line becomes 'durch mein Lektorat bei der Vorbereitung und'. The remaining run is a separate selectable object.
allFindings.evidence: textCount 106 -> 105 (one run removed) and screenshot exp-pdf-text-edit2-E-delete.png shows the line now reads 'durch mein Lektorat bei der Vorbereitung und' with 'Ich entlaste' gone. DOM: 112 layer children all <g>, each a single short run (e.g. ' ', 'Dr. Maria B.', 'www.swiftLin'). A logical paragraph/line is split across many independent objects.
allFindings.impact: Even the operations that DO work (delete, move) are unusable for real editing because the unit of selection is an arbitrary glyph/word fragment, not a sentence or line. Moving one fragment would break line alignment; deleting leaves orphaned remainders. Makes meaningful manual cleanup impractical.

allFindings.title: Text tool over existing text creates a new empty run and silently loses typed input
allFindings.repro: Open editable PDF, press T, click directly on existing text, type a correction, press Escape. A new empty text edit is started at the click point (state.text reset to ''), the existing run is not loaded, and the typed correction does not appear in the document (text run count did not increase with content; original unchanged).
allFindings.evidence: textTool.ts startEditing() (lines 216-224) unconditionally sets state.text='' and creates a fresh <text>; onMouseDown (269-279) always calls startEditing regardless of what is under the cursor — it never reads/edits an existing run. Scenario: after T-click + type 'Typo fix' + Escape, last 3 runs were [' ',' ',' '] and the original text was unchanged; C-texttool export render unchanged.
allFindings.impact: Misleads users who reasonably expect the Text tool to let them click into existing text and retype. Input is silently discarded — data-loss-adjacent UX with no feedback.

allFindings.title: No double-click-to-edit handler on canvas selection
allFindings.repro: Open editable PDF, Select tool, double-click any text run. Nothing happens beyond a normal single selection of the <g>; no inline editor, no caret, activeElement stays BODY.
allFindings.evidence: selectTool.ts contains no dblclick/onDoubleClick handling (grep for dblclick/doubleClick/detail in selectTool returns nothing). Probe: B) dblclick -> {selBoxes:1, activeTag:'BODY', editing:false, inspectorHead:'G · 1 SELECTED'}; typing after dblclick changed no text.
allFindings.impact: The single most discoverable affordance for entering text edit mode (double-click) is absent, reinforcing that there is no route to text editing. Users will conclude the PDF text is uneditable.

allFindings.title: mostly-outlined badge never shows when outlined PDF is imported via primary 'Open PDF...' (feature defeated on the main path)
allFindings.repro: Fresh app -> File > Open PDF... -> select 'Flyer Swift Vortragscoaching yellow BG bluer Border.pdf'. Wait for render. Observe Layers panel: layer is still named 'Layer 1' with NO warning badge, even though the DOM layer has data-mostly-outlined=true, data-path-count=216, data-text-chars=15. Compare: importing the SAME PDF via 'Open PDF as Background Layer...' DOES show the badge.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario stats Step 3: layer {textChars:'15', pathCount:'216', mostlyOutlined:'true'} but badges:0 and name 'Layer 1'. Step 5 (background path) for same PDF: badges:1, name 'Flyer Swift...', mostlyOutlined:'true'. Confirmation script: 'IMMEDIATELY AFTER primary import of outlined PDF: {badges:0, domMostlyOutlined:true}' then 'AFTER forcing a panel refresh (add-layer click): {badges:1}'. Root cause: pdfImport.ts applyParsedSvg() calls clearSelection() at line 310 (its first statement) BEFORE removing old layers and inserting new ones; clearSelection() synchronously fires the selection notification (selection.ts:77) which is the LayersPanel's refreshLayers trigger, so the panel reads stale layer state and never refreshes after the new badge-tagged layer is inserted. importPdfAsBackgroundLayer's applyParsedAsBackgroundLayer deliberately calls clearSelection() LAST (pdfImport.ts:302 with an explicit comment) which is why the badge appears there.
allFindings.impact: A user opening an outlined/print PDF the normal way gets zero indication that the text is non-editable paths. They will try to edit text, fail, and have no explanation. The whole mostly-outlined detection feature is silently dead on the most common import path.

allFindings.title: After 'Open SVG...' the Layers panel shows phantom layers that no longer exist in the document (stale panel)
allFindings.repro: Build a composite (Open PDF... then Open PDF as Background Layer...) so the panel lists two layers. Then File > Open SVG... -> select any SVG (e.g. test/golden/milestones/fixtures/02-filled-circle.svg). The canvas correctly replaces everything with the SVG content, but the Layers panel STILL lists the two old layers ('Flyer Swift Vort...' with its warning badge + 'Layer 1') that were removed from the DOM.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario Step 7 stats: DOM has layerCount:1, single 'Layer 1' with 1 child (the circle), viewBox reset to '0 0 210 297' (correct replace). But panelText still reads '...Flyer Swift Vortragscoaching yellow B... (warning) ... Layer 1 ...' and badges:1. Screenshot exp-pdf-import-07-open-svg.png shows canvas = lone green circle while the panel shows two layer rows including the warning badge. Same root cause as finding 1: fileio.ts applyParsedSvg() calls clearSelection() FIRST (fileio.ts:411) before removing/adding layers, so the panel never refreshes to the new single-layer reality.
allFindings.impact: Panel layer rows reference detached/removed DOM nodes. Clicking visibility/lock/reorder/delete on a phantom row operates on dead elements (no-op or error). The user sees layers that aren't there and is missing the actual current layer's correct name. Confusing and a source of follow-on corruption.

allFindings.title: PDF/SVG import is not undoable; a stray re-Open silently destroys edited work with no recovery
allFindings.repro: Open PDF... (or Open SVG...) to load content. Press Ctrl+Z. Nothing is undone. Separately: 'Open PDF...' a second time replaces (clears) all existing layers; combined with no undo, any edits made after the first import are lost permanently with no way back.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario Step 4: after importing the outlined PDF (218 layer children) and pressing Ctrl+z, stats show the layer still has 218 children and unchanged viewBox '0.00 0.00 210.02 297.01' (the import was not reverted). Code: importPdf/importPdfAsBackgroundLayer (pdfImport.ts) and importSvg (fileio.ts) mutate doc.svg directly and never call history.execute / push a Command, so the undo stack has no entry. Step 1->Step 2 confirms re-Open is destructive replace (layer children stayed 112, old content gone, new content in).
allFindings.impact: Data-loss vector: import then edit then accidentally trigger another Open (or the same import) -> work gone, Ctrl+Z cannot recover. For a vector/PDF editor this is a serious safety gap.

allFindings.title: Place Image after a background-layer import drops the image onto the hidden bottom layer (invisible)
allFindings.repro: Open PDF... (primary editable), then Open PDF as Background Layer... (outlined). Now File > Place Image... -> select a PNG. The image is added but does not appear on the canvas.
allFindings.evidence: Scenario Step 6: imageEls on the BOTTOM 'Flyer Swift...' background layer went 1->2 (kids 218->219) while the foreground 'Layer 1' (editable flyer on top) is unchanged at imageEls:3. Screenshot exp-pdf-import-06-place-image.png is visually identical to the pre-place composite; the placed 32x32 PNG is hidden behind the full-page foreground content. Root cause: placeImage (fileio.ts:321) uses doc.getActiveLayer(); after the stale-panel background import, getActiveLayer (document.ts:100-105) falls back to layers[0] which is the bottom/background layer, so the image lands behind everything.
allFindings.impact: User places an image and it silently vanishes. Tied to the same stale active-layer state caused by findings 1/2. Confusing; user may place repeatedly or assume Place Image is broken.

allFindings.title: Primary 'Open PDF...' import does not name the layer after the file (always 'Layer 1'), unlike background import
allFindings.repro: Open PDF... any file. The layer is named 'Layer 1'. Open PDF as Background Layer... names the layer after the file (e.g. 'Flyer Swift Vortragscoaching yellow B...').
allFindings.evidence: Scenario Step 1/3: primary-import layer name stays 'Layer 1'. Step 5/8: background-import layer named 'Flyer Swift Vortragscoaching yellow B...'. In pdfImport.ts applyParsedSvg (primary) there is no setAttribute('data-layer-name', ...) / sanitizeLayerNameFromFile call, whereas applyParsedAsBackgroundLayer sets it (line 288).
allFindings.impact: Inconsistent UX; a multi-import workflow yields generic layer names with no provenance. Minor.

allFindings.title: Document Setup / change page size does nothing - viewBox and artboard never update
allFindings.repro: 1) Open app (fresh A4 doc). 2) File > Document Setup. 3) Click A3 preset (or type Width=500, Height=400, or click Square 100). 4) Click Apply. EXPECTED: artboard + viewBox + rulers resize to the new size. ACTUAL: nothing changes - viewBox stays '-10 -10 230 317', the white artboard rect stays width=210 height=297, rulers unchanged. Reproduces even on a brand-new empty document (no content drawn).
allFindings.evidence: Drill output: initial {viewBox:'-10 -10 230 317', artboard:{w:'210',h:'297'}} -> after apply 500x400 {viewBox:'-10 -10 230 317', artboard:{w:'210',h:'297'}}; viewBox reflects 500x400? false; artboard rect resized? false. Square 100 also no-op. Main run: dialog correctly showed width=297/height=420 after A3 preset, but post-Apply viewBox/artboard unchanged and screenshots exp-save-open-05-after-resize.png is pixel-identical to before. Post-resize Export SVG still has viewBox=-10 -10 230 317.
allFindings.impact: A whole advertised feature (Document Setup / artboard sizing, the dialog the journey is named after) is non-functional. Users cannot change page size at all. Exports are locked to A4.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: src/components/ArtboardDialog.tsx onApply -> src/App.tsx (onApply={setDimensions} at line ~426) -> src/components/Canvas.tsx effect lines 142-150 calls computeDocumentBounds() which reads the artboard model (src/model/artboard.ts bounds()). No code calls updateArtboard()/addArtboard with the new dimensions, so model bounds never change and the viewBox/artboard-rect stay at init values.

allFindings.title: Text edit mode swallows tool-shortcut keystrokes instead of switching tools (corrupts text + drops intended actions)
allFindings.repro: 1) Press T (text tool), click canvas, type 'ABC'. 2) Without pressing Escape, press 'r' (rect tool shortcut). ACTUAL: active tool stays 'text' (no switch); the 'r' is consumed by the text editor. In the main journey, typing 'RoundTrip!' then pressing v then p (intending select then pen) produced the literal text 'RoundTrip!vp' and the pen path I tried to draw never got created (layer kids = rect + text only, no path). Pressing Escape first, THEN 'r', correctly switches to rect.
allFindings.evidence: Drill: 'After typing ABC then pressing r: activeTool= text'. Main run AFTER DRAW snapshot: text#vf-2 txt="RoundTrip!vp" (the v+p leaked in) and only 2 layer kids - the intended pen path is absent. Workaround confirmed: 'After Escape then r: activeTool= rect'.
allFindings.impact: Tool shortcuts silently corrupt text content and silently no-op the intended tool action while a text element is being edited. Easy to hit, produces garbage text and lost work with no error.
allFindings.rootCauseFile: src/tools/text tool keyboard handling / global shortcut dispatcher (text edit mode does not yield single-letter tool shortcuts; shortcut handler should be suppressed only for printable text but must still allow tool switching, or text edit must commit/blur on tool-shortcut)

allFindings.title: SVG export->Open SVG round-trip is lossless (positive finding)
allFindings.repro: Draw rect + text, File > Export SVG, then File > Open SVG of the exported file.
allFindings.evidence: viewBox before/after identical (-10 -10 230 317); kids count 2->2; ids stable (vf-1,vf-2 == vf-1,vf-2); per-kid attrsEqual=true and txtEqual=true for both rect and text including full float precision (x=-3.8201234340667725 etc); export contained no leaked overlay/grid/guides groups (overlay leaked? false); 0 console/page errors. PNG export (33617 bytes) rendered clean and matches canvas, correctly clipped to artboard.
allFindings.impact: Round-trip and PNG paths are trustworthy - no data loss or id drift. This part is solid and should not be touched.

allFindings.title: Status-bar +/- zoom buttons are completely dead (no handlers wired)
allFindings.repro: Open app. Click [data-role="zoom-in"] twice, then [data-role="zoom-out"]. Read the SVG viewBox width and zoom percent before/after.
allFindings.evidence: Script output: 'zoom-in x2: 120% -> 120% | vb.w 230 -> 230' and 'zoom-out x1: 120% -> 120% | vb.w 230 -> 230'. The viewBox never changes. Root cause: src/App.tsx:416 renders <StatusBar cursorX cursorY zoomPercent /> with NO onZoomIn/onZoomOut props, so StatusBar's onClick handlers (StatusBar.tsx:109,107) are undefined. The buttons also carry cursor:'default' (chipBtnStyle, StatusBar.tsx:29) so they don't even look interactive. The only way to zoom is the mouse wheel.
allFindings.impact: The single most discoverable zoom UI in the app does nothing. Trackpad/touch users with no scroll-wheel, and anyone who clicks the obvious +/- buttons, cannot zoom at all.

allFindings.title: Plain mouse-wheel scrolling always zooms; no scroll-to-pan, no Ctrl gate
allFindings.repro: Open app, hover over the canvas, scroll the wheel WITHOUT holding Ctrl (page.mouse.wheel(0,-120) x3).
allFindings.evidence: Script output: 'PLAIN wheel(-120)x3 (NO ctrl): vb.w 230 -> 172.8 actual 119.9 -> 159.5'. Root cause: src/components/Canvas.tsx:233-240 handleWheel calls e.preventDefault() then zoomAtPoint() unconditionally; grep for ctrlKey/metaKey in Canvas.tsx returns nothing. Standard editors zoom only on Ctrl+wheel and pan/scroll on plain wheel. Here plain wheel zooms and there is no scroll-pan path at all (pan is only middle-drag or space-drag).
allFindings.impact: Every casual scroll gesture rockets the zoom in/out unexpectedly. Users cannot scroll a tall document; the expected scroll-to-pan interaction is absent, and accidental zoom is the default behavior.

allFindings.title: Displayed zoom percent lies at startup (shows 100% while actually ~120%); true 100% is unreachable
allFindings.repro: Open app. Before moving the mouse, read the status-bar percent vs the real zoom (svg.clientWidth / viewBox.width / (96/25.4)).
allFindings.evidence: Script output: 'INITIAL actual: actualPct 119.9, vbw 230, clientW 1042 statusbar shows: 100%'. After a single mousemove the status corrects to '120%'. The initial viewBox is computeDocumentBounds() = page+10mm padding = 230x317 fit into a 1042px pane = 4.53 px/mm = 119.9% of the 96-DPI natural 3.78 px/mm, but StatusBar defaults zoomPercent=100 (StatusBar.tsx:54 / App.tsx state default zoomPercent:100) and that stale value is shown until emitState fires on mousemove. The initial screenshot confirms the ruler reads 0..200mm across the pane (~5 px/mm) yet the pill says 100%. There is also no control that maps to an exact 100%.
allFindings.impact: The zoom readout is wrong on load and misleads the user about scale; combined with zpv-4 there is no way to get to a known 100%/actual-size.

allFindings.title: No Fit / 100% / Actual-Size / Reset-zoom affordance anywhere; View menu has no zoom items
allFindings.repro: Open the View menu. Search the whole DOM for any fit/actual-size/reset/zoom-to-fit text. Try keyboard zoom (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0).
allFindings.evidence: Script output: 'View menu visible items (filtered): ["Toggle GridCtrl+'","Outline Mode","Add Horizontal Guide...","Add Vertical Guide...","Clear All Guides"]' and 'Any fit/actual-size/reset affordance found in DOM text: false'. App.tsx:174-189 confirms the View menu has only grid/outline/guides. There is no keyboard zoom binding (grep finds zoom only in the wheel handler). Once a user has scrolled to an arbitrary zoom (e.g. 1571% or 4%), there is no command to return to fit-page or 100%.
allFindings.impact: Standard, expected zoom commands (Fit, 100%/Actual Size, Zoom In/Out via keyboard) are entirely missing. After getting lost at an extreme zoom the user has to manually wheel back, with the dead +/- buttons offering no help.

allFindings.title: Zoom clamp constants misinterpreted: actual range ~3.5%..1571% instead of documented 10%..6400%
allFindings.repro: Hover canvas, wheel-out ~40 steps to hit the floor, then wheel-in ~90 steps to hit the ceiling; read actual percent.
allFindings.evidence: Script output: 'ZOOM-OUT FLOOR: actualPct 3.5, pxPerUnit 0.133' and 'ZOOM-IN CEILING: actualPct 1571.5, pxPerUnit 59.394'. src/model/zoom.ts:3-4 declares MIN_ZOOM=0.1 ('10% of natural') and MAX_ZOOM=64 ('6400% of natural'), but line 50-51 compares svg.clientWidth/newWidth (raw px-per-mm) against those constants. Since 100% == 3.7795 px/mm, the real limits are MIN 0.1/3.7795 ~= 2.6% and MAX 64/3.7795 ~= 1693% (observed 3.5% / 1571% due to the 1.1x step granularity). The clamp does not normalize to the natural DPI the comments claim.
allFindings.impact: Achievable zoom range is roughly 3.5x narrower at the top end than documented and the floor is far below the intended 10%, letting the artboard shrink to a few pixels. Mostly cosmetic/edge-case but the constants don't mean what they say.

allFindings.title: POSITIVE: coordinate mapping, ruler tracking, and hit-testing are accurate at all zoom levels and after pan
allFindings.repro: Draw a rect; convert its doc-center to screen via the live CTM; click it at 100%, after wheel-zoom-in (~430%), and after a space-drag pan; also click near the rect corner. Move cursor to a known doc point and read the mm status.
allFindings.evidence: Status mm readout exact: 'moved to doc(105.0,148.5) ... status reads X=105.0 Y=148.5'. Hit-tests: 'HIT @100% center -> selBoxes 1', 'HIT @zoomed-in rect-center -> selBoxes 1', 'HIT @rect near-corner -> selBoxes 1', and after pan selBoxes=1. Ctrl/anchored wheel keeps the doc point under cursor fixed: 'doc-under-cursor before {x:105,y:148.5} after {x:105,y:148.49}'. Rulers verified visually at 4%, 120%, and 1571% showing correct mm spans (e.g. 118..134 at 1571%). screenToDoc/docToScreen in src/model/coordinates.ts use getScreenCTM() which is inherently correct.
allFindings.impact: The historically fragile coordinate-space core is in good shape; no hit-test drift found at non-100% zoom or near edges. This is the salvageable foundation under the broken zoom chrome.

allFindings.title: Eraser drag across multiple shapes: undo throws and restores nothing (permanent data loss)
allFindings.repro: 1) Draw 3 separate rects in a row. 2) Pick Eraser (E rail slot). 3) Press mouse down on the left rect and drag horizontally across all 3, release. All 3 are erased (layer children 3 -> 0). 4) Press Ctrl+Z. Result: nothing is restored (children stay 0) and a pageerror is thrown. 5) Ctrl+Y (redo) also does nothing. The 3 shapes are gone with no recovery. NOTE: single-click erase of ONE shape undoes correctly (2 -> 3); only the multi-element drag is broken.
allFindings.evidence: drill stdout: 'before drag erase kids: 3' -> 'after drag erase kids: 0' -> 'after undo drag erase kids: 0 (expected back to 3 )' -> 'after redo kids: 0'. Screenshot /home/tobias/Projects/vectorfeld/test/review/shots/exp-misc-tools-10-undo-drag-erase.png shows only one rect remaining after undo.
allFindings.impact: Core destructive operation with no undo = data loss. A user who drag-erases and changes their mind cannot recover their work.

allFindings.title: Rail labels Eraser shortcut as 'E' but pressing E activates the Ellipse tool
allFindings.repro: 1) Look at the left rail: the eraser slot displays 'E' under it. 2) Click empty canvas, press the 'E' key. Active tool becomes 'ellipse', NOT eraser. 3) The eraser's real shortcut is 'x' (pressing X activates eraser). The overflow menu even lists Ellipse with shortcut 'E' too. So 'E' is doubly advertised and resolves to ellipse.
allFindings.evidence: stdout: "pressed 'e' -> active tool = ellipse (rail labels E as eraser)"; "pressed 'x' -> active tool = eraser". Source: LeftRail.tsx line 26 declares { key: 'erase', shortcut: 'E' } while eraserTool.ts line 35 has shortcut: 'x', and ellipseTool.ts line 75 has shortcut: 'e'.
allFindings.impact: A user pressing the advertised key gets the wrong tool and may erase nothing / draw an ellipse unexpectedly. Misleading UI label.

allFindings.title: Status-bar 'Saved' dot is hardcoded green and never reflects unsaved edits
allFindings.repro: 1) Make many destructive edits (draw, erase, flip, delete). 2) Observe the status-bar dot: still green, label still 'Saved'. It never turns to an unsaved/dirty state.
allFindings.evidence: stdout: 'saved indicator text after many edits: "Saved"' and savedDotColor rgb(74,168,90) (green) after dozens of edits. Source: StatusBar.tsx lines 74-78 set background:'#4aa85a' as a literal with no dirty-state prop.
allFindings.impact: False assurance — user believes work is saved when it never was. Misleading persistence signal.

allFindings.title: Status-bar page-navigation arrows are permanently disabled stubs
allFindings.repro: Inspect [data-role=page-nav]: both prev (◂) and next (▸) buttons have disabled=true and the text is a fixed 'Page 1 / 1'. They never enable even with multi-page documents reachable elsewhere in the app.
allFindings.evidence: stdout: pageNavButtons [{text:'◂',disabled:true},{text:'▸',disabled:true}], pageNavText 'Page 1 / 1'. Source StatusBar.tsx lines 84-88 hardcode disabled buttons and 'Page 1 / 1'.
allFindings.impact: Dead widget; page navigation must happen via the right-panel Pages tab instead. Inconsistent/confusing UI.

allFindings.title: Selecting an overflow tool gives no active-state indication in the rail
allFindings.repro: 1) Open the ⋯ overflow menu, pick Ellipse/Line/Pencil/Measure/Lasso/Scale. 2) The chosen tool is active (confirmed via registry: getActiveToolName returns it) and works, but NO rail slot shows data-active='true' and the overflow button itself is not highlighted. The user has no visual cue which tool is currently active.
allFindings.evidence: stdout shows e.g. 'ellipse active: ellipse' and shapes draw correctly, but state() reports activeTool:null (rail data-active) throughout the overflow-tool phase. LeftRail.tsx only sets data-active on RAIL slots, never on OVERFLOW_TOOLS.
allFindings.impact: Discoverability/feedback gap. Combined with the orphaned-from-rail placement, the powerful tools (ellipse/line/pencil/measure/lasso/free-transform) feel hidden and stateless even though they fully work.

allFindings.title: POSITIVE/correction: overflow tools (ellipse, line, pencil, measure, lasso, free-transform) are all functional, not orphaned

Screenshots exp-misc-tools-16-ellipse-draw.png, -17-line-draw.png, -18-pencil-draw.png, -19-measure-drag.png, drill2-lasso.png, drill2-ft.png.

allFindings.title: File > Open PDF... silently destroys the entire current document and is NOT undoable (data loss)
allFindings.repro: 1. Draw any content (e.g. 3 rects) — layerKids=3. 2. File > Open PDF... and pick test/dogfood/fixtures/'Flyer Swift Vortragscoaching 15.04.2026 noheader.pdf'. 3. Observe canvas now shows ONLY the PDF (112 elements); the 3 rects are gone (not 115 — replaced, not merged). 4. Press Ctrl+Z. Nothing happens: layerKids stays 112, selection unchanged. The user's prior work is permanently unrecoverable.
allFindings.evidence: exp-chaos-pdf.mjs log: existing content {layerKids:3} -> after import {layerKids:112} -> undo after import {layerKids:112} (unchanged). Screenshots exp-chaos-pdf-01-imported.png (only flyer, no rects) and exp-chaos-pdf-03-undo.png (undo is a no-op, full PDF still present). Root cause in src/model/pdfImport.ts applyParsedSvg(): line 316-318 'for (const layer of doc.getLayerElements()) layer.remove()' deletes all existing layers via raw DOM, and importPdf() (line 167-196) never goes through CommandHistory.execute, so the wipe+import is invisible to undo.
allFindings.impact: A user with an in-progress drawing who chooses 'Open PDF...' (reasonable mental model: open a PDF to trace/annotate) instantly loses all their work with no undo and no confirmation dialog. Pure, silent data loss from a top-level File menu action.

allFindings.title: Stale selection after undo-to-empty lets a Delete wipe the redo stack -> permanent loss of undone work
allFindings.repro: 1. Draw 3 rects. 2. Ctrl+A (3 SELECTED). 3. Ctrl+Z x6 until canvas is empty (layerKids=0). Inspector STILL says '3 SELECTED' with 3 phantom selection-boxes over empty canvas. 4. Press Delete on the phantom selection -> selection clears (no visible change, canvas already empty). 5. Press Ctrl+Shift+Z (redo) x6 -> NOTHING comes back; the 3 rects are gone forever.
allFindings.evidence: exp-chaos-phantom.mjs log: 'UNDO-TO-EMPTY phantom: {layerKids:0, selBoxes:3, insp:"3 SELECTED 3 items..."}' then 'after Delete: {layerKids:0, selBoxes:0, NO SELECTION}' then 'after redo x6 from phantom: {layerKids:0}'. Contrast exp-chaos-redo.mjs / exp-chaos-undo2.mjs where redo works perfectly (Ctrl+Shift+Z restores everything) when no spurious command is issued. Mechanism: CommandHistory.execute() (src/model/commands.ts:39) does 'this.redoStack = []' on every new command; the phantom selection tricks the user into issuing a Delete command, which legitimately clears redo and strands the undone work. Root issue is undo() not clearing/validating selection (src/model/commands.ts undo() lines 43-49 + selection state).
allFindings.impact: Escalates the previously-known cosmetic stale-selection bug into real data loss: a natural 'oops, delete this leftover selection' reflex after over-undoing permanently destroys the redo history. No console error, completely silent.

allFindings.title: Undo to empty canvas leaves phantom selection boxes + 'N SELECTED' inspector (known #1, re-confirmed and characterised)
allFindings.repro: Draw shapes, Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+Z past the point where all shapes are gone. layerKids=0 but selBoxes>0, 8 scale-handles render, and inspector shows 'N SELECTED' (or 'G · 1 SELECTED vf-<timestamp>' if the prior ops included grouping) with all geometry fields 0.00.
allFindings.evidence: exp-chaos2.mjs P7: 'UNDO-TO-EMPTY: {layerKids:0, selBoxes:1, scaleHandles:8, inspector:"G · 1 SELECTED vf-1782076838042 ..."}'. exp-chaos-phantom.mjs: '{layerKids:0, selBoxes:3, insp:"3 SELECTED"}'. Screenshot exp-chaos2-05-undo-empty.png shows a dashed selection box with 8 handles around an empty area, inspector 'G · 1 SELECTED vf-1782076838042', X/Y/W/H all 0.00, Layer 1 empty.
allFindings.impact: Confusing dangling selection that points at a deleted/timestamp-id'd phantom element; on its own cosmetic, but it is the precondition for the data-loss finding exp-chaos-phantom-delete-wipes-redo.

allFindings.title: Dragging a guide from the ruler into the canvas never creates a guide (dead feature) and H-ruler passes wrong axis coordinate
allFindings.repro: 1. Press-drag from the horizontal ruler strip (top, ~y73 screen) downward into the canvas and release. 2. No horizontal guide appears. Same for the vertical ruler dragged rightward.
allFindings.evidence: exp-chaos-drill9.mjs: guide count stays 0 after both H-ruler and V-ruler drags. Root cause src/components/Ruler.tsx: guide creation lives in handleMouseUp bound as React onMouseUp on the <canvas> ruler element (line 173/291), but the gesture releases the mouse OVER the SVG canvas, not over the ruler, so the React synthetic onMouseUp never fires. Additionally HRuler.handleMouseUp (lines 156-162) computes docX (an X coord) and calls addGuide('h', docX) — a horizontal guide is defined by a Y coordinate, so even if it fired the value would be wrong (and the comment 'For now, create at a position derived from cursor / we need doc coords' flags it as unfinished).
allFindings.impact: A discoverable affordance (rulers with guide-drag cursor) does nothing; minor since guides are a secondary feature, but the code is both unreachable and computing the wrong axis.

allFindings.title: Ctrl+Y (common redo shortcut) is not bound — redo only available via Ctrl+Shift+Z
allFindings.repro: Draw shapes, Ctrl+Z to undo, then press Ctrl+Y -> nothing happens. Ctrl+Shift+Z works.
allFindings.evidence: exp-chaos-redo.mjs: after one undo (kids=4), Ctrl+Y leaves kids=4 (no-op); Ctrl+Shift+Z correctly redoes. Source: src/model/EditorContext.tsx only handles redo at lines 119-121 (Ctrl+Shift+Z); no 'y' handler exists. (Note: this is also why my first undo-storm pass appeared to show 'redo broken' — it was using Ctrl+Y; redo itself is fully functional.)
allFindings.impact: Windows users who expect Ctrl+Y for redo will think redo is broken. Pure shortcut-coverage gap, easy fix.

allFindings.title: Export emits 'Font cannot be both symbolic and non-symbolic. Skipping subsetting.' (known #5)
allFindings.repro: Import the editable flyer PDF, then File > Export PDF. Console logs the warning.
allFindings.evidence: exp-chaos2.mjs and exp-chaos-pdf.mjs console: 'warning: Font cannot be both symbolic and non-symbolic. Skipping subsetting.' This was the ONLY console output across the entire chaos run — no other errors/warnings under heavy stress.
allFindings.impact: Font subsetting skipped on export (larger output / potential glyph fidelity); pre-existing known issue.
